scope_note: Covers the statutory powers available to the Scottish Ministers to establish a bus fare cap operating nationally in Scotland, and distinguishes those powers from the concessionary travel scheme powers that are often confused with them. Limited to legislation (Acts and SSIs); case law and the policy history of any particular scheme are out of scope in this mode.

steps.title: Identify the Scottish Ministers' powers to fund bus services
steps.detail: Find the provisions of the Transport (Scotland) Act 2001 that let the Scottish Ministers make grants to bus operators or for transport purposes generally, and establish whether those grants may be made subject to conditions determined by Ministers.

steps.title: Establish whether any provision confers an express fare-capping power
steps.detail: Check the Transport (Scotland) Act 2001 and the Transport (Scotland) Act 2005 for any provision empowering the Scottish Ministers to set, cap or otherwise control the fares charged to passengers generally, as distinct from funding operators.

steps.title: Set out the concessionary travel scheme powers and how they differ
steps.detail: Retrieve the national and local travel concession scheme powers (section 68 of the Transport (Scotland) Act 2001 and section 40 of the Transport (Scotland) Act 2005), including the statutory definition of a travel concession, and identify what those schemes do that a fare cap does not.

steps.title: Confirm how a national scheme is made in practice
steps.detail: Take a national travel concession scheme made by order and confirm from its own text which enabling power it was made under and what rate of concession it sets, as a worked example of the concessionary route.
